case.title: CrSBr, field-driven reversal
case.reason: The kickoff material and, because of its triaxial anisotropy, the natural host of the biaxial cost-reduction mechanism.
case.expectation: The optimal pulse cost falls with switching time toward the universal floor; the hard axis pushes the numerical cost below the free-macrospin floor.

material.name: CrSBr
material.easy_axis: in-plane b axis (triaxial: b easy, z hard)
material.notes: Monolayer, ferromagnetic within a layer, antiferromagnetically stacked in bulk. The exchange Hamiltonian is measured by inelastic neutron scattering (Scheie 2022, S = 3/2), but the anisotropy is below the neutron resolution; the easy-axis scale and the hard-axis ratio used here are assumed and flagged. Triaxiality and its dielectric tunability are computed (Rudenko 2023): the substrate is a knob on the hard axis.

moment.note: S = 3/2 Cr(III) from the neutron Hamiltonian, g = 2.

anisotropy.note: Below neutron resolution. Chosen at the scale of the quoted zone-centre magnon gaps (0.102 and 0.141 meV); a ferromagnetic gap-to-K relation does not hold for the antiferromagnetically stacked bulk. Kept because manuscript M1 uses it.

hard_axis_ratio.note: Triaxiality (b easy, z hard) is computed; the ratio of the hard to the easy scale is an assumption.

damping.note: The typical value set in first-principles spin dynamics of CrSBr; no measurement found.
